questions.q: TCP/IP is a set of rules (protocols) that allows devices to communicate over the internet.
HTTP encrypts all data that is sent between a browser and a website.
questions.explain: HTTP does not encrypt data; HTTPS does.

questions.q: In a peer-to-peer network all computers have equal status and no central server is needed.
A DDoS attack tries to overwhelm a server with so much traffic that it becomes unavailable.
The protocol SMTP is used for ____ email.
The rules that allow devices to communicate with each other are called ____.
Scrambling data so that it cannot be understood if it is intercepted is called ____.
An attack that floods a server with requests so it cannot respond to real users is a ____ of ____ attack.
Explain how a file is sent across the internet as packets.
questions.answer: The file is split into packets (1); each packet has an address/number and may take a different route (1); the packets are reassembled in the correct order at the destination (1).

questions.q: State two differences between a client-server network and a peer-to-peer network.
questions.answer: Any two from: client-server has a central server but peer-to-peer does not; client-server is easier to manage/secure centrally; peer-to-peer computers share resources equally; client-server is usually more expensive to set up.

questions.q: Explain why HTTPS is more secure than HTTP.
questions.answer: HTTPS encrypts the data (1) so that anyone who intercepts it cannot read it (1).
